questions.q: What single feature of the data distinguishes supervised from unsupervised learning?
options: The number of columns
Whether the dataset is stored in a database
Whether the training data includes the answer (label) you want to predict
Whether the features are numeric
questions.explain: Supervised learning has labeled examples. Unsupervised learning has only features and no answer column.

questions.q: Predicting whether a customer will churn (yes or no) is an example of:
options: Supervised classification
Supervised regression
Clustering
Dimensionality reduction
questions.explain: There is a known outcome column and it is a category, so this is supervised classification.

questions.q: Predicting next month's sales revenue as a dollar amount is an example of:
options: Clustering
Unsupervised learning
Classification
Supervised regression
questions.explain: The label is a number, which makes it a supervised regression problem.

questions.q: KMeans returns cluster labels 0, 1 and 2. What do those numbers mean?
options: They are arbitrary group names; only which rows share a group matters
Cluster 0 is always the largest group
They match the true class numbers exactly
They rank groups from best to worst
questions.explain: Cluster IDs are arbitrary. Rerunning with a different seed can number the same groups differently.

questions.q: Why is judging an unsupervised model harder than judging a supervised one?
options: Unsupervised models are always less accurate
There is no ground-truth label to compare predictions against, so interpretation takes human judgment
Unsupervised models cannot be fitted with scikit-learn
They require more rows than supervised models
questions.explain: Without a known answer there is nothing to score against directly, so you judge whether the groups are useful and sensible.
